contexts.title: Defined C and a bounded record tool
contexts.problem: A record is useful only if every byte access, lifetime and arithmetic operation is defined. Establish these obligations before selecting a container.

contexts.title: Ordered records and bounded lookup
contexts.problem: Filtering, deduplication and range queries demand explicit comparator and ownership contracts. Compare linear scans, sorted views and hashing on the same records.

contexts.title: Incremental input and owned publication
contexts.problem: File, socket and device input arrives in fragments. A finite queue must preserve unread bytes, expose pressure and publish only complete records.

contexts.title: Configuration, symbols and reusable interfaces
contexts.problem: Configuration keys and runtime symbols need stable identity while storage may move or rehash. Distinguish equality, address identity and ownership.

contexts.title: Deadlines, dispatch and overload
contexts.problem: An event service must find due work, cancel stale registrations and bound retention. A changing operation mix motivates a representation change.

contexts.title: Allocation and durable indexed storage
contexts.problem: A growing store must account for allocation failure, fragmentation, page I/O and recovery. A successful in-memory update is not durable publication.

contexts.title: Compilation and dependency processing
contexts.problem: Build dependencies, control flow and incremental computation form graphs. Cycles, reachability and fixed points impose different contracts.

contexts.title: Telemetry and numerical processing
contexts.problem: A stream of observations needs bounded history, stable numerical meaning and honest uncertainty. Select summaries using the query and error contract.

contexts.title: Concurrent state and machine boundaries
contexts.problem: Sharing a component changes the proof: publication order, borrower lifetime and reclamation become separate obligations.

contexts.title: Firmware and kernel integration
contexts.problem: Portable mechanisms meet reset, interrupt, DMA and ABI contracts. Preserve freestanding boundaries and qualify every reused artifact on its consumer target.

contexts.title: Native measurements and causal diagnosis
contexts.problem: A timing difference must survive equal semantics, generated-code inspection and a defensible observation boundary. Hardware events answer narrower questions than their names suggest.

contexts.title: Independent system selection and transfer
contexts.problem: An unfamiliar service workload must be decomposed into explicit contracts. Select and reject mechanisms using evidence, then revise them under a changed assumption.
